PATH FORWARD, ONLINE.
A proposal for the redesign and rebuild of CTW's website.

To our friends at CTW,

We are excited to present our proposal to redesign and rebuild CTW's online presence. The plan closes the gap between the firm CTW has become and the digital surface that still represents it, and positions the firm for the way prospects will find accounting firms over the next decade.

Three engagement modes give CTW choice over how deep the partnership goes. Path Forward Foundation is the rebuild itself, ready in four weeks. Path Forward Engine adds a content production system that fills the new site with work that compounds. Path Forward Partnership runs the full ongoing program with quarterly business reviews and continuous content production.

A few elements worth calling out:

The four-week core delivery commitment. Most professional services website rebuilds run six to nine months. We deliver in four. The velocity comes from a content extraction and rewriting pipeline we have built and refined on prior projects, paired with a senior team that runs the work directly without handoffs. I built MKTNG's AI infrastructure myself, including GoldenDoodle AI, our trauma-informed communications platform, so the pipeline behind this delivery is something we own and tune, not something we license.

What comes after launch. Most agencies sell a website and disappear. We do not. The Engine and Partnership tiers are built around the work that actually moves the needle for a professional services firm over time. A podcast that opens doors with the people CTW wants to know. Original research that gets cited. A press release program that compounds in AI search. Partner LinkedIn programs that build personal authority alongside the firm's brand. We have produced this kind of work for clients across professional services, infrastructure, and energy for more than a decade. Most of our client relationships run two, three, or more years.

The Capital Event Readiness Assessment. An AI-powered lead generation tool that delivers a custom-written readiness report to qualified prospects, written in CTW's voice, specific to their actual business. The conversion data on this approach is meaningfully better than the gated PDF most professional services firms still use.

We also recommend professional photography of CTW's partners, staff, and office space. Stock photography is the most common way professional services websites communicate they were built quickly. CTW deserves better than that. Photography integrates without delaying the four-week core launch, with the public launch landing at eight weeks if photography is elected.

We are confident this plan will produce a modern, high-performing online presence that reflects the firm CTW already is internally and gives the team a platform that earns its keep across the next decade.

We look forward to discussing this proposal with you further.

Scott Eggert
President, MKTNG

The work does not end at launch. Sustaining a site with content that compounds, in a partner's voice, across years, is what most firms skip and most agencies do not sell. Producing podcasts that turn guest interviews into lasting relationships. We are not the cheapest agency CTW will hear from. We do not intend to be the most expensive. Section 1

Reading the Moment

CTW's recent work tells a clear story. Capital events for middle-market owners. Quality of earnings studies for buyers. Tax structuring for sellers. FAR compliance for government contractors. Multi-state audits for manufacturers and distributors. The firm is good at high-stakes, multi-year, advisory-led engagements.

You already know the current website doesn't reflect any of that. A few things we picked up in the initial review:

  • The home hero rotates between four messages with no anchoring position
  • The services architecture lists roughly sixty offerings across four pillars
  • The industries page names twenty-eight verticals, which is the opposite of specialization
  • The newsroom's most recent post is from 2020
  • The firm is still labeled "Campbell Taylor Washburn" in page metadata and footers, despite the rebrand

This is lag, not failure. Most professional services websites run two or three years behind the firms they represent. Running an accounting practice doesn't leave time to rebuild a digital surface every year. The opportunity right now is to close the gap. To take the firm CTW already is internally and make it visible externally.

The market is moving in CTW's favor. AICPA data shows advisory-led firms commanding higher pricing and more durable client relationships than compliance-led peers. The recent Moss Adams and Baker Tilly merger consolidated mid-tier national firms in a way that creates space for sharper regional players. Generative AI is reshaping how prospects find firms. ChatGPT alone now drives close to two percent of all search traffic, up from a quarter of a percent twelve months ago. Firms that get cited by AI answer engines today are building moat for tomorrow.

CTW has the substance. The website is what gets it cited.

Section 3

Approach and Methodology

The four-week core commitment is real because the work behind it is staged. Each phase has a defined input, a defined output, and a clean handoff to what follows. The velocity comes from a content extraction and rewriting pipeline we built and refined on prior projects, including GoldenDoodle AI, MKTNG's own trauma-informed communications platform. The pipeline is something we own and tune, not something we license. The longer engagement modes extend this same process into the year after launch, with the same senior team running the work throughout.

Phase 0: Brand and Messaging Sprint (Week 1)

A focused four-hour working session with CTW's leadership locks the firm's position, the value proposition, and the audience-specific framings for the four prospect types: business owners, CFOs, PE sponsors, and capital markets prospects.

The output is delivered in two formats. A printed reference document for CTW's internal use. And a Claude Voice Skill: a structured AI prompt artifact that captures CTW's voice attributes, audience-specific framings, vocabulary patterns, and tone variations. The skill loads into any current AI writing tool and produces on-brand content from the moment it is installed. CTW keeps the skill permanently. Anyone at the firm can use it. The skill does not degrade or expire. As AI tools evolve, the skill upgrades with them.

Most agencies deliver brand voice as a PDF that gets opened twice and then forgotten. We deliver brand voice as a working tool that anyone at CTW can use to generate on-brand content for the next ten years.

Phase 1: Architecture, Content Audit, and AEO Foundation (Week 2)

The existing site gets audited page by page, with a documented retain, rewrite, or retire recommendation against each one. The AEO baseline expands from the eight queries we ran during proposal preparation to twenty-five priority queries mapped to CTW's actual practice areas and named geographies. Sitemap gets finalized jointly with CTW's leadership. Schema architecture is defined. The technical foundation on Astro, Cloudflare, and Keystatic initializes in parallel with the audit so no time is lost.

The content audit generates the initial 301 redirect map in parallel. Every page marked for consolidation or retirement receives a redirect destination before development begins. SEO continuity is not an afterthought managed at launch. It is an output of the audit itself, reviewed and confirmed with CTW before a single page changes.

Phase 2: Design and Content Production (Week 3)

Joshua presents three design directions to CTW's leadership for selection. The chosen direction becomes the component library and visual system for the full site. Content rewrite begins on the priority pages identified in the audit. Where CTW writes, we edit and structure for AEO. Where we write, the copy runs through the brand voice document so the firm's tone holds throughout. CTW reviews all content before it goes live.

Phase 3: Build, Integration, and QA (Week 4)

Development runs against the approved design and audited content. Calendar booking integrates with Microsoft 365. The Capital Event Readiness Assessment, the two calculators, and the CPACharge payment flow all connect. Accessibility testing runs against WCAG 2.2 AA. The site goes to soft launch for CTW's leadership review at the end of the week. CTW selects one design direction by end of week three to hold the four-week delivery commitment.

Phase 4: Launch, Training, and Stabilization (Week 5 and Beyond)

Public launch with 301 redirects mapped from old URLs, search consoles submitted, and analytics confirmed. The four CTW content stewards complete a single live training session on Keystatic, with a recorded video and a one-page reference card for follow-up. Performance monitoring stays active through ninety days of stabilization support. This is the point at which most agencies end their engagement. Ours doesn't.

Phase 5: Ongoing Partnership (Engine and Partnership Tiers)

For CTW selecting the Engine or Partnership modes, Phase 5 extends the engagement into the full ongoing program: the content production cadence documented in Section 7, the quarterly business reviews and competitive monitoring detailed in Section 13, and the proactive strategic input that keeps the engagement generating value past the first year. The senior team that ran the build runs the ongoing program. No handoffs.

The site architecture this process produces is detailed in Section 4.

Section 4

Recommended Site Architecture

The architecture below represents a full professional services site of twenty-seven to thirty-six indexed pages, built around three principles. Clarity for the visitor, who should reach any service, industry, or tool in one or two clicks from anywhere on the site. AEO depth at every page that matters, with structured FAQ blocks, schema markup, and plain-language content built for direct citation by AI search engines. And forward-rebrand readiness, so a future identity change propagates across the site without page-by-page rework.

This is a substantively different scope than the current site. It is not a refresh of eight pages. It is a new site built to perform like a category leader: individual pages for each partner, dedicated service-detail pages for each practice area, a developed Insights structure, and lead-generation tools with their own indexed landing pages.

Final selections within the architecture, particularly the short list of named industries and the exact partner page roster, happen jointly during the brand sprint. The structure here reflects our best recommendation given what we know about the firm's current trajectory.

Notes on the Architecture

The previous version of this site treats Team as a subsection of About. That structure works for a two-partner firm with nothing to say. CTW has eight partners and a bench of senior staff, each with decades of focused experience. Visitors who care about capital event readiness, construction audit work, or government contracting want to know who specifically they are going to work with. Burying partner bios under About tells prospects that the people are an afterthought. Giving TEAM its own top-level section, with individual pages for each partner and key senior staff, signals the opposite. It also gives each partner page its own AEO surface, which means CTW's people become individually citable by AI search engines answering questions like "who handles construction company audits in Sacramento."

SERVICES carries the most structural change. The current site lists Consulting as the top-level catch-all, with Transaction Services and Capital Markets buried underneath it. That's backwards for a firm whose most differentiated and high-value work is in advisory and capital events. Transaction Services and Capital Markets get their own pillar at the same level as Audit, Tax, and Consulting. Each of the four pillars becomes a hub page with four to six dedicated service detail pages below it. A service detail page for "R&D Tax Credits" or "Cost Segregation Studies" isn't just a navigation endpoint. It's a standalone AEO retrieval target that answers the specific question a CFO is asking before they ever think about calling an accountant. The difference between a site with one SERVICES page and a site with twenty-three to twenty-seven service-detail pages is the difference between one shot at a citation and twenty-three.

INDUSTRIES consolidates from twenty-eight to three to five named verticals. The current breadth signals a generalist practice that will work with anyone, which is exactly not how CTW's best clients find them. Vertical specificity in the navigation matches the way CTW actually wins engagements. The final industry list is selected during the brand sprint, with CTW's leadership making the call based on recent advisory and capital event work. The candidates are construction and infrastructure, manufacturing and distribution, real estate, government contractors, and professional services firms.

INSIGHTS replaces the existing Newsroom, which contains posts from 2019 and 2020, most of which reference regulations that have since changed. The new structure has four sections: Articles, Podcast, Original Research, and Press Releases. Final retain, rewrite, and retire decisions on existing content happen jointly during the content audit. CTW preserves authority over what stays. Nothing gets archived without sign-off.

TOOLS is a new top-level section. Each tool, the Capital Event Readiness Assessment, the R&D Tax Credit Estimator, and the Cost Segregation Estimator, gets its own indexed page because each one is a discrete AEO retrieval target. Calculator-style queries carry real search volume. A dedicated page gives each tool a legitimate shot at direct citation. A tool buried in a form field on the Contact page does not.

CLIENT TOOLS and LEGAL live in the footer. Pay Invoice and the ShareFile portal link belong where existing clients expect to find them, not competing with prospect-facing navigation for attention in the primary menu. The legal pages, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Cookie Policy, and Accessibility, are present and discoverable but do not consume navigation real estate.

A CMS Built for Non-Developers

Keystatic gives CTW's four content stewards a web-based editor that reads like a modern document tool: rich text, image uploads, drag-and-drop reordering, version history, preview before publish. Routine updates (a new team member, a newsroom post, a service description revision) take minutes, not tickets. When larger development support is needed, the codebase is structured so any competent developer can ship the change quickly. CTW receives a maintainable system, not a black box.

Forward-Rebrand Architecture

CTW's leadership flagged in the Q&A that a future full rebrand may happen. Brand tokens (name references, logos, color palettes, typography) live as configuration variables, not values hardcoded into pages or components. When the rebrand happens, a designer updates the token file, the system rebuilds, and the new identity propagates across the entire site in under an hour. This is how the build is structured on day one, not a feature scoped later.

CRM-Ready Data Layer

The website operates as if a CRM is already in place. Every form, calculator, assessment, and calendar booking writes to a unified event schema mapped to HubSpot and Salesforce contact properties. For most CPA firms of CTW's stage, we recommend HubSpot as the entry point: the free tier is genuinely useful, the paid tiers cost an order of magnitude less than Salesforce, the marketing automation is serviceable out of the box, and HubSpot's recently launched native AEO tracking tools integrate cleanly with the AEO foundation. Salesforce becomes the right call when the firm is ready to integrate deeply with audit workflow software or scale beyond fifty staff. The day CTW signs the CRM engagement letter, migration is days rather than weeks, and the lead generation system does not pause.

A note on WordPress. WordPress remains a solid choice for many use cases. For CTW's specific requirements (performance, AEO discoverability, ease of content updates, security with minimal maintenance, forward-rebrand flexibility), the plugin ecosystem creates ongoing fragility, the hosting overhead is unnecessary, and the performance ceiling is lower than what the stack delivers.

Why You Will Not Be Stranded

We build the infrastructure we promise rather than deploying off-the-shelf platforms. The Capital Event Readiness Assessment, the AI Concierge, the lead routing system, and the AEO foundation are systems we own at the architecture level, refined and shipped on prior projects. The codebase CTW receives is a maintainable system, not a stack of plugins we hope continues to work.

1. Calendar Booking with Intelligent Routing

Calendly Teams integrates across the site with a three-question qualifying form (inquiry type, timeline, current client status) that routes prospects to the right partner or senior manager. Capital event inquiries reach the Capital Markets practice. Audit and tax inquiries route to the matching practice lead. Existing clients route to a separate path so current relationships do not enter the prospect funnel. Calendly integrates natively with Microsoft 365 and Outlook, which is what CTW already uses.

2. Capital Event Readiness Assessment

This is the highest-leverage lead generation tool in the package. It replaces what most professional services firms still do (gated PDFs that anyone can download) with something materially better: a custom-written report generated for the prospect's actual business.

Here's how it works. A business owner on the site, somewhere in the two-to-five-year window before a sale or recapitalization, clicks "Get your readiness assessment." They answer eight to ten structured questions about their business: industry, revenue range, ownership structure, anticipated transaction type, timeline, current advisory situation, financial reporting maturity. Two open-ended fields capture context.

The submission triggers a workflow that calls Claude (or GPT-4) against a structured rubric we develop in the brand sprint with CTW's Capital Markets practice. The rubric defines what a good readiness story looks like, what the common gaps are at each business size and stage, and what the recommended next steps are based on the inputs. The AI generates a custom-written assessment in CTW's brand voice. Two to three pages. Specific to that prospect's situation.

The assessment lands in the prospect's inbox as a branded HTML email within minutes of submission. They get something written for them, not for a category. The submission and output are stored for sales follow-up, a notification fires to the firm's preferred internal channel, and a conversion event is logged for attribution.

Three things make this work that competitors won't replicate quickly. The output is delivered as a branded HTML email, not a downloadable file, so the perceived value sits with the firm that produced it. The custom-written content is materially more valuable than a generic guide, which raises the brand value of the firm behind it. And the architecture supports rapid expansion: once the first assessment is proven, we can spin up additional versions (audit readiness, tax planning health check, succession readiness) using the same plumbing.

3. Live Calculators

Two embedded calculators ship with the Foundation tier and are designed for both AEO retrieval and lead capture. The R&D Tax Credit Estimator takes industry, wage base, supplies, and contract research inputs and produces a defensible federal credit estimate, capturing prospect email at the detailed-report step. The Cost Segregation Benefit Estimator takes property type, purchase price, building basis, and year placed in service to produce a benefit projection. Both keywords have real search volume and convert at materially higher rates than average site traffic. Additional calculators (Section 199A QBI, Quality of Earnings checklist, business valuation rough cut) are available in the Engine and Partnership tiers.

4. AI Concierge (Engine and Partnership Tiers)

A conversational AI assistant trained on CTW's published content, service descriptions, and partner bios. Site visitors ask questions in natural language and receive answers in CTW's voice within seconds; when intent is clear, the assistant offers calendar booking and routes to the appropriate practice. The concierge runs on the same Cloudflare infrastructure as the Capital Event Readiness Assessment, with a vector store holding embeddings of CTW's content, and operates at fifty to two hundred dollars per month at expected traffic. The result is a 24/7 prospect engagement layer that most regional CPA firms will not have for at least two more years.

5. CRM-Ready Architecture

CTW does not have a CRM yet, and the website operates as if it does. Every form, calculator, assessment, and calendar booking writes to a unified event schema; server-side tracking captures form submissions, page views, and engagement signals; UTM discipline is enforced on every external campaign link. Visitor profile data sits in a structured database ready to be replayed into HubSpot, Salesforce, or whichever CRM CTW selects. The day CTW signs the CRM engagement letter, migration is days rather than weeks, and the lead generation system does not pause.

6. Visitor Identification

RB2B identifies individual US-based business visitors at the person level, not just the company level. When a prospect at a target firm visits CTW's Capital Markets practice page, the right CTW partner receives a notification with the visitor's name, title, and LinkedIn profile within minutes. The free tier is sufficient to start; the paid tier ($299 per month, paid directly by CTW if elected) expands identification volume. The capability inverts the old assumption that you cannot follow up with someone who did not fill out a form. Most regional CPA firms will not have this layer for at least two more years.

Section 7

Content Engine and AEO Strategy

Most CPA firm websites treat content as a launch deliverable. Write the pages, ship the site, move on. The result is what the rest of the industry now looks like. Pages from 2019 about regulations that have since changed. A newsroom that goes silent six months after launch. A LinkedIn presence run by someone other than the people who actually do the work.

CTW's website should be the opposite. Built to be filled, not just built to be launched. The content engine that follows is the system that does the filling. Some pieces we produce. Some pieces CTW produces. The discipline is shared.

The technical work matters. Schema markup, structured FAQ blocks, site speed under one second on every page, semantic HTML for AI retrieval, every service page architected to be cited by an answer engine. AEO compliance is the price of admission, and other bidders will deliver it.

What's harder, and what most firms get wrong, is the sustained human work behind the technical foundation. A partner's voice in writing across a year. A podcast that builds genuine relationships, not download counts. Press releases that say something rather than fill space. Original research that the firm actually conducts, with its actual clients, producing actual findings. The discipline to ship this work weekly, quarterly, annually, without losing the thread.

Every piece of new content added to the site after launch is registered in the sitemap and cross-referenced against the 301 redirect map. No URL goes live without a forward path if the content ever moves. This protects the SEO equity the site accumulates over time.

This is what we've spent more than a decade learning how to do.

Section 8

Trust, Compliance, and Accessibility

Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA conformance is built in from the start: semantic HTML, passing contrast ratios at every type size, full keyboard navigation, visible focus states, and screen reader compatibility validated against NVDA and VoiceOver before launch. We do not install accessibility widget overlays. Those products do not satisfy WCAG and have been the basis of recent ADA lawsuits. The site itself is accessible, backed by a published accessibility statement page with testing documentation and a direct contact path for any visitor who finds an issue.

Privacy and Data Handling

The existing CTW privacy policy is dated 2020 and predates current California Privacy Rights Act requirements. The rebuild includes a modernized privacy policy drafted against current CCPA standards. All form data, assessment submissions, and calendar booking details travel encrypted with TLS and are stored encrypted at rest. Cookie consent surfaces for visitors in regulatory environments. Analytics run server-side where possible. All visitor data lives on infrastructure CTW controls.

Security Posture

Cloudflare provides DDoS protection, web application firewall, bot mitigation, automatic SSL, and edge-level rate limiting as part of the infrastructure. The static site architecture removes the most common attack vectors: no SQL database to inject, no PHP runtime to exploit, no plugins requiring constant patching. The security posture is published alongside the privacy and accessibility statements. Middle-market buyers and CFOs read these pages, and a modern security posture stated plainly is a differentiator in a category where most firms say nothing.

Section 12

Success Metrics

The site is instrumented from launch day to track lead generation, user engagement, SEO and AEO performance, and site effectiveness, with monthly written briefs and live quarterly reviews against a baseline established in the first thirty days.

What We Track

Lead Generation

  • Calendar bookings: volume, conversion to held meetings, downstream pipeline value
  • Capital Event Readiness Assessment completions and follow-up engagement
  • Calculator completions and email capture rates
  • Newsletter subscribers (monthly net growth)
  • Inbound contact attribution by channel (organic, AEO citation, direct, referral, paid)

User Engagement

  • Sessions, unique visitors, returning visitors
  • Pages per session and depth-of-engagement signals
  • Scroll depth on long-form content
  • Conversion paths: which pages appear before a form submit

SEO and AEO Performance

  • Organic search rankings for priority queries (monthly)
  • Organic traffic by landing page, attributed to specific content investments
  • Core Web Vitals scores across every page, sustained green at launch and ongoing
  • AEO citation tracking against named competitors across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews (quarterly; baseline established in Section 7)
  • Press release pickup and citation in AI search results

Site Effectiveness

  • Page-by-page conversion rates
  • Bounce rates by page type
  • Completion versus abandonment for calendar booking, assessment, and calculators
  • Mobile versus desktop behavior splits

What We Expect

A performance baseline will be established in the first thirty days post-launch. Specific targets will be set jointly with CTW leadership against that baseline. Realistic ranges based on similar engagements:

  • Organic search traffic: 200 to 400 percent growth over the existing baseline within twelve months, driven by AEO foundation, content velocity, and improved Core Web Vitals
  • AEO citation rate (currently 50 percent across the eight queries we baselined): targeted to 75 percent or better within twelve months, with a particular focus on closing the gap on ChatGPT and Grok where CTW currently underperforms
  • Calendar booking conversion: industry benchmark for professional services is 1 to 3 percent of qualified site visitors; we target the higher end of that range with the routing system in place
  • Capital Event Readiness Assessment completion: target completion rate of 35 to 50 percent of users who initiate the assessment; target email capture of 90 percent or better at completion
  • Newsletter list growth: target of 50 to 100 net new subscribers per month after the first quarter

These are forecasts, not guarantees. We refine them quarterly based on observed performance.

How We Report

  • Monthly: Written brief on top-line metrics, notable shifts, and any operational items needing CTW's attention.
  • Quarterly: Live business review covering performance, AEO citations against competitors, lead funnel analysis, content review, and the next-quarter recommendation list. Two named MKTNG leaders attend.
  • Annually: End-of-year strategic review with cumulative results, ROI analysis, and recommendations for the next year.

Instrumentation

The website ships with PostHog product analytics, Cloudflare edge metrics, server-side conversion tracking, and a custom quarterly AEO citation protocol against a named competitor set. When CTW selects a CRM, the data layer is already mapped to receive events and reporting consolidates into the CRM's native dashboards plus the quarterly review.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

This section addresses questions that typically come up during proposal evaluation. If your question isn't here, please contact us directly.

Can you really deliver the core website in four weeks?
Yes. The four-week timeline assumes the engagement letter is signed by May 18, 2026 and CTW selects one of three design directions by end of week three. Original photography, if elected, extends the timeline to eight weeks. The compressed schedule is achievable because of three things: an AI-assisted content extraction and rewriting process we've developed and used on prior projects, a technology stack that doesn't require the configuration overhead of WordPress, and a senior team that runs the work directly without handoffs.
What happens if CTW's leadership wants to change the design direction mid-build?
The Astro and Keystatic architecture isolates content from presentation. Design changes in the early build phase are quick. Major design changes post-launch are scoped as separate work. We will surface design decision points clearly during the engagement so changes happen at the right time, not after launch.
How does this work with our future CRM?
The website's data layer is structured to map cleanly to HubSpot or Salesforce on day one of CRM rollout. Forms, calculators, calendar bookings, and assessment completions all write to a unified event schema. Migration to a CRM takes days, not weeks. We recommend HubSpot for CTW's stage.
Will our team be able to update the site without calling MKTNG?
Yes. Keystatic is designed for non-developers. The four trained content stewards at CTW will manage routine updates (newsroom posts, team changes, service description revisions, event listings) without developer involvement. Larger changes (new sections, new lead generation tools) are scoped as supplemental work.
What does the relationship look like after launch?
Determined by the engagement mode. Foundation includes ninety days of stabilization support and a light maintenance retainer. Engine adds twelve months of structured content production. Partnership runs as an ongoing strategic communications partnership with quarterly business reviews, AEO citation tracking, and continuous content production. CTW can move between modes as needs evolve.
What if CTW pursues a full rebrand in the future?
The site is built rebrand-ready. Name references, logo files, color palettes, and typography are isolated as configuration. A future rebrand propagates across the entire site in under an hour once the design tokens are updated. No page-by-page rework required.
How do we know your AEO claims are real?
We ran a baseline AEO analysis as part of preparing this proposal. CTW currently appears in fifty percent of the test queries we ran across five major AI search engines, with significant gaps on the engines holding the largest market share (ChatGPT and Grok). Full results are included in Section 7 and Appendix A. We track quarterly improvement against this baseline as part of the Engine and Partnership tiers.
What's the typical client tenure with MKTNG?
Most of our client relationships run two to three years or longer. Some have been with us since the firm's founding. Long-tenured client relationships are how the work compounds and how the firm operates sustainably.
How is pricing structured across the three engagement modes?
Each mode has a one-time build investment and (in the Engine and Partnership tiers) an ongoing monthly retainer. Detailed pricing is in Section 11. We are happy to walk through the line items in any follow-up conversation.
How will success be measured?
We track lead generation metrics (form submissions, calendar bookings, assessment completions, calculator engagement), user engagement metrics (traffic, depth of engagement, conversion path analysis), SEO and AEO performance (organic rankings, traffic, AEO citation tracking against named competitors), and site effectiveness (page-level conversion rates). Reporting is monthly in writing and quarterly in live business reviews. Full framework is detailed in Section 12.
Why are you recommending against WordPress?
For most use cases, WordPress is fine. For CTW's specific requirements (performance, AEO discoverability, ease of content updates, security with minimal maintenance, forward-rebrand flexibility), the plugin-ecosystem fragility, hosting overhead, and performance ceiling make it the wrong tool. We address this in detail in Section 5.
What's different about MKTNG compared to other agencies CTW will hear from?
Three things. We deliver in four weeks, not six to nine months. We run strategy, design, build, and ongoing content as one senior team rather than handing off between specialists. And we treat the engagement as a multi-year communications partnership rather than a one-time website project. Most of our clients stay for years.
